questions.stem: What size range defines a nanoparticle?
questions.explanation: Nanoparticles are typically defined as particles with dimensions between 1 and 100 nanometres (nm). 'Nano' means one billionth, so 1 nm = 1 x 10⁻⁹ m.

questions.stem: Why do nanoparticles have different properties compared to the same material in bulk form?

options.text: Because they are made of different atoms
Because they have a very high surface area to volume ratio

questions.explanation: Nanoparticles have a very high surface area to volume ratio compared to bulk materials. This means a much greater proportion of their atoms are on the surface, which changes their properties such as reactivity and colour.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a use of nanoparticles in medicine?

options.text: Targeted drug delivery to specific cells

questions.explanation: Nanoparticles can be used to deliver drugs directly to specific cells in the body, such as cancer cells. This can reduce side effects and make treatments more effective.

questions.stem: What happens to the surface area to volume ratio as particles get smaller?
questions.explanation: As particles get smaller, the surface area to volume ratio increases. This is because volume decreases more rapidly than surface area as size decreases.

questions.stem: Silver nanoparticles are used in some wound dressings and deodorants. Why?

options.text: Because they make the products waterproof
Because silver nanoparticles have antibacterial properties
Because silver is shiny and attractive
Because they are the cheapest material available

questions.explanation: Silver nanoparticles have antibacterial properties, meaning they can kill bacteria. Their high surface area to volume ratio makes them particularly effective at this.

questions.stem: Why are some scientists concerned about the widespread use of nanoparticles?

options.text: Because they make products less effective
Because their long-term effects on health and the environment are not fully understood

questions.explanation: There are concerns about nanoparticles because they are so small they could enter cells and the bloodstream. Their long-term effects on human health and the environment have not been fully researched.

questions.stem: Nanoparticles of titanium dioxide are used in sunscreen. What advantage do they have over larger particles?

options.text: They are completely safe with no risks
They provide better UV protection and appear transparent on the skin

questions.explanation: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles effectively block UV radiation while being so small that they appear transparent on the skin, unlike larger particles which leave a visible white layer.
